notes.text: The continuing main argument says that the relevant elements are conjugate for x varying in a connected component D_{J,alpha}, and that choices can make the exterior-automorphism indeterminacy in (39) come from the displayed component extension group. This reports the manuscript’s assertion; no theorem has been independently established here.

For J={i}, the author inserts “dans ce cas d’ailleurs D_J=D_i” over cancelled wording, followed by live “est” and connexe with a possible diaeresis over its first e. Formula (40) gives the map labelled kappa_i from T to pi_{U/K}^{bar L}. The following claim is that its exterior homomorphism is well determined and compatible with the indicated exterior operations. The source’s “mod autom intérieurs près” is retained without stylistic repair.

The upper margin explains choices of universal covers over the fixed barred K and ends in a two-object group diagram. The lower note qualifies the geometric definition modulo inner automorphisms and discusses invariance of the exterior homomorphisms with the exterior “cyclotomique” action on T^J. The tiny covering superscript and two small word endings remain paleographic doubts; their intended mathematical values have not been supplied.

The entire last paragraph is cancelled by large crosses. Within it, a raised inclusion of barred D strata and a locally cancelled intersection remain separately visible revision layers. The original nonemptiness parenthesis uses the phi-shaped empty-set sign. The final sentence stops after “une comp. conn.” on this sheet; nothing is completed from an expected continuation.

The handwritten (39) is an inline reference in the prose, while (40) labels the following displayed map. The short strokes beneath “et” and “sur” are the two overbars of the inserted D symbols below, so et receives no underline. Thin foliation 135 is recorded separately without confidently assigning it to the main hand. No additional authorial question or demonstrable mathematical slip has been asserted from this page alone.

All 18 saved first-pass crops were visually inspected. P13 and P14 are rotated inspection images of the two oblique notes; all recorded boxes remain coordinates in the original 1679 by 2359 scan. The full image and both supplied halves were each read once before these crop decisions. No OCR, external research, proof computation or TeX compilation was used.

audit_changes.evidence: Two detached accent strokes and the looped l are secure. After the tall final t, a long low exit ends in a downward curl; that curl can be s or a terminal return. The oblique stroke below the opening belongs to the margin.

The detached overbar is clear; beneath it several horizontal retracings join a left upright, a heavy lower foot and a diagonal right branch. They can represent an overwritten L/K or a cancelled K, but no separate cancellation line extends beyond this glyph. The body must stay in the superscript position.

The word begins with low c/o bodies before a tall h. A separate accent follows, then low r/e/n joins and a final crossed t with an e exit. Habile would require an initial h and a late uncrossed l, which these strokes do not show. Alpha, the apostrophe and the cedilla are also visible.
